Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
2 October 2026 .
Brent $ 99.63 -1.40 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 TradeWinds News and Investing.com Australia report a projectile of unknown origin struck a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on October 1, igniting a fire, with crew reported safe.

02 Brent stood at $99.63, down 1.40% over 24 hours, as of 14:56 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

03 Caspian Post reports Iran is moving to restrict military cargo ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the site of sustained and escalating attacks on commercial shipping. TradeWinds News and Investing.com Australia report that a projectile of unknown origin struck a tanker in the strait on October 1, igniting a fire; crew are reported safe. Caspian Post reports Iran is moving to restrict military cargo ships in the strait. A gCaptain account from a tanker captain describes veering around a struck vessel already on fire and contacting the US Navy. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $99.63, down 1.40% over 24 hours, as of 14:56 UTC. The attacker has not been publicly identified in any of the current incident reports, and no US or independent authority has attributed responsibility for the October 1 or September 29 strikes. As of 14:50 UTC, 189 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, rising over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
